senses.en: Needing a lot of workers.

ex.en: Harvesting tea is labor-intensive work.
ex.zh: 采茶是劳动密集型工作。

senses.en: The choice and style of words in speech or writing.
The way someone pronounces words, especially how clearly.

ex.en: Her formal diction sounded strange at our relaxed picnic.
ex.zh: 在我们轻松的野餐聚会上，她正式的措辞听起来很不协调。

ex.en: Writers often adapt their diction to make complex scientific ideas accessible to a wider audience.
ex.zh: 作者常会调整措辞，让更广泛的读者能够理解复杂的科学概念。

tip: 既可指用词风格，也可指吐字是否清晰。

senses.en: The use of machines to do work once done by hand or by animals.

ex.en: Mechanization transformed agriculture.
ex.zh: 机械化改变了农业。

senses.en: The amount of material or work that passes through a system in a given time.

ex.en: The new machines doubled the factory's throughput.
ex.zh: 新机器使工厂的产量翻了一番。

senses.en: A point where a process slows down because of a limitation.

ex.en: A shortage of chips created a bottleneck in car production.
ex.zh: 芯片短缺造成了汽车生产的瓶颈。

senses.en: a part of a rock formation visible above the ground

ex.en: We climbed a rocky outcrop.
ex.zh: 我们爬上一处裸露的岩石。

ex.en: Geologists study outcrops along road cuts because they reveal layers of rock that are normally hidden underground.
ex.zh: 地质学家研究公路边坡上的露头，因为它们显露出平时埋在地下的岩层。

tip: 野外地质常用词。

senses.en: Comparing performance with the best in an industry.

ex.en: Benchmarking showed where the company was falling behind.
ex.zh: 标杆对比揭示了公司落后的地方。

senses.en: An estimate of how much something is worth.

ex.en: The startup reached a valuation of one billion dollars.
ex.zh: 这家初创公司估值达到10亿美元。

senses.en: Priced or rated higher than its real worth.

ex.en: Analysts said the shares were overvalued.
ex.zh: 分析师说这些股票估值过高。

senses.en: An extremely strong feeling of joy and delight.

ex.en: The children watched the dancing dolphins in rapture.
ex.zh: 孩子们欣喜万分地看着海豚跃动。

ex.en: The rapture experienced during live performances helps explain why audiences continue to value shared cultural events.
ex.zh: 现场演出带来的强烈喜悦，有助于解释观众为何依然珍视共同参与的文化活动。

col: go into raptures over｜对……欣喜若狂
tip: 语气强于happiness，常带文学色彩。

senses.en: Not given as much value or respect as it deserves.

ex.en: The currency was undervalued by about 20%.
ex.zh: 这种货币被低估了约20%。

senses.en: A person who puts money in a bank.

ex.en: Depositors rushed to withdraw their money.
ex.zh: 存款人争相取钱。

senses.en: Unable to pay debts.

ex.en: The bank was declared insolvent.
ex.zh: 这家银行被宣布无力偿债。

senses.en: Making something false seem true or something unreal seem real.

ex.en: The mirror created a delusive impression of extra space.
ex.zh: 这面镜子造成了空间更大的错觉。

ex.en: Early economic gains may create a delusive sense of security if governments ignore underlying weaknesses in public finances.
ex.zh: 如果政府忽视公共财政的潜在弱点，早期经济收益可能造成虚假的安全感。

col: delusive sense of security｜虚假的安全感
tip: 较正式且少见；日常多用misleading或deceptive。

senses.en: The state of a company being run by an official because it cannot pay its debts.

ex.en: The airline went into receivership.
ex.zh: 这家航空公司进入破产管理程序。

senses.en: Closing a business and selling its assets to pay debts.

ex.en: The firm went into liquidation last year.
ex.zh: 该公司去年进入清算。

senses.en: having soft, loose flesh rather than firm muscles
lacking strength, effectiveness, or clear structure

ex.en: He felt his muscles had grown flabby during recovery.
ex.zh: 他觉得自己的肌肉在康复期间变得松弛了。

ex.en: An essay with flabby arguments may fail to persuade readers, even when its topic is important.
ex.zh: 即使主题重要，论证松散无力的文章也可能无法说服读者。

tip: 多指肌肉松弛；形容文章时指松散无力，语气贬义。

senses.en: To close a business and sell what it owns; to turn assets into cash.

ex.en: The owners decided to liquidate the company.
ex.zh: 业主决定清算公司。

senses.en: Taking back a property because the borrower failed to repay the loan.

ex.en: Thousands of homes faced foreclosure.
ex.zh: 成千上万的房屋面临止赎。

senses.en: To take back property when a loan is not repaid; to rule out a possibility.

ex.en: The bank foreclosed on the farm.
ex.zh: 银行收回了农场。

senses.en: a device measuring the total distance a vehicle has travelled

ex.en: The odometer showed how far we had driven.
ex.zh: 里程表显示了我们已经行驶的距离。

ex.en: When purchasing a used vehicle, consumers should check its odometer reading alongside its maintenance records.
ex.zh: 购买二手车时，消费者应将里程表读数与保养记录一并核查。

tip: 记录累计里程；speedometer显示即时车速。

senses.en: Taking back goods or property when payments are not made.

ex.en: Missed payments led to the car's repossession.
ex.zh: 拖欠付款导致汽车被收回。

senses.en: A legal right to keep someone's property until a debt is paid.

ex.en: The bank holds a lien on the house.
ex.zh: 银行对这栋房子享有留置权。

senses.en: Money or property held by a third party until conditions of a deal are met.

ex.en: The deposit is held in escrow until the sale closes.
ex.zh: 定金由第三方托管，直到交易完成。

senses.en: To strongly urge someone to do something.

ex.en: Our coach exhorted us to keep trying until the end.
ex.zh: 教练力劝我们坚持努力到最后。

ex.en: Public health campaigns exhort citizens to exercise regularly, but affordable facilities are also needed to support lasting change.
ex.zh: 公共卫生宣传敦促市民经常锻炼，但要支持持久的改变，也需要价格亲民的设施。

col: exhort someone to act｜敦促某人行动
exhort citizens to vote｜敦促公民投票
tip: 正式用词：exhort sb to do，不只是提出忠告。

senses.en: A person who judges the value of property or goods.

ex.en: An appraiser valued the painting at $10,000.
ex.zh: 一位估价师给这幅画估价一万美元。

senses.en: A person whose job is to help sell or rent houses and land.

ex.en: The realtor showed them three houses.
ex.zh: 房产经纪人带他们看了三套房子。

senses.en: Owning a property for a fixed period under a lease.

ex.en: The flat is sold on a 99-year leasehold.
ex.zh: 这套公寓以99年租赁产权出售。

senses.en: The practice or study of writing and editing dictionaries.

ex.en: My aunt works in lexicography and loves discussing words.
ex.zh: 我姑姑从事词典编纂工作，很喜欢讨论词语。

ex.en: Digital lexicography allows dictionary editors to track changes in language through large collections of authentic examples.
ex.zh: 数字词典编纂使编辑能够通过大量真实用例追踪语言变化。

col: a career in lexicography｜词典编纂职业
tip: 指词典编纂或其研究，通常作不可数名词。

senses.en: Full ownership of land or property for an unlimited time.

ex.en: They bought the freehold of the building.
ex.zh: 他们买下了这栋楼的永久产权。

senses.en: The change of a poor area as wealthier people move in, often pushing up costs.

ex.en: Gentrification forced many long-time residents to move.
ex.zh: 中产阶级化迫使许多老居民搬走。

senses.en: appearing real but based on illusion

ex.en: The desert shimmered with illusive pools of water.
ex.zh: 沙漠中闪现着虚幻的水洼。

ex.en: Advertising may create an illusive sense of happiness by linking personal fulfilment exclusively to material possessions.
ex.zh: 广告可能将个人满足感完全与物质财富挂钩，从而营造出虚幻的幸福感。

tip: 较少用，常用illusory；elusive意为难以捉摸的。

senses.en: A system that limits total pollution and lets companies buy and sell permits.

ex.en: A cap-and-trade scheme reduced sulfur emissions.
ex.zh: 总量管制与交易制度减少了硫排放。

senses.en: The habit of using money carefully.

ex.en: Her thriftiness allowed her to save a lot.
ex.zh: 她的节俭让她存了很多钱。

senses.en: The profit a government makes by issuing money.

ex.en: Seigniorage is a hidden source of state revenue.
ex.zh: 铸币税是国家收入的一个隐性来源。

senses.en: A sequence formed by selecting elements without changing their original order.

ex.en: We selected alternate beads to create a subsequence.
ex.zh: 我们隔一颗选一颗珠子，组成了一个子序列。

ex.en: Researchers can analyse a subsequence of genetic data to identify patterns associated with inherited diseases.
ex.zh: 研究人员可以分析遗传数据的子序列，以识别与遗传病有关的模式。

tip: 主要是数学、计算机术语；“后果”用consequence。

senses.en: More of something than is needed or wanted.

ex.en: An oversupply of oil pushed prices down.
ex.zh: 石油供过于求压低了价格。

senses.en: Caring about others and acting to help them without expecting reward.

ex.en: Animals such as dolphins show signs of altruism.
ex.zh: 海豚等动物表现出利他行为的迹象。

senses.en: The relationship in which one event makes another happen.

ex.en: Correlation does not prove causation.
ex.zh: 相关性不能证明因果关系。

senses.en: the study of fossils and ancient life

ex.en: She wants to study paleontology.
ex.zh: 她想学古生物学。

ex.en: Advances in paleontology, such as CT scanning, let researchers see inside fossils without breaking them.
ex.zh: CT扫描等古生物学进展让研究人员不用破坏化石就能看到内部。

col: vertebrate paleontology｜脊椎动物古生物学
tip: paleo-（古）+ onto（存在）+ logy。

senses.en: The outer layer of the brain, involved in thought and perception.

ex.en: The visual cortex processes what we see.
ex.zh: 视觉皮层处理我们看到的东西。

senses.en: A chemical that carries signals between nerve cells.

ex.en: Serotonin is a neurotransmitter linked to mood.
ex.zh: 血清素是一种与情绪有关的神经递质。

senses.en: A brain chemical that helps control mood and sleep.

ex.en: Low serotonin levels are linked to depression.
ex.zh: 血清素水平低与抑郁有关。

senses.en: To walk with short, unsteady steps, especially as a young child.
To walk somewhere casually and without hurrying.

ex.en: The baby toddled across the rug towards her father.
ex.zh: 宝宝摇摇晃晃地走过地毯，朝爸爸走去。

ex.en: As children begin to toddle, safe spaces allow them to develop balance and explore their surroundings independently.
ex.zh: 孩子开始蹒跚学步时，安全的空间能让他们练习平衡，并独立探索周围环境。

col: toddle across the room｜蹒跚着穿过房间
toddle towards someone｜蹒跚走向某人
tip: 主要作不及物动词；学步幼儿叫toddler。

senses.en: A brain chemical involved in pleasure and reward.

ex.en: Rewards trigger the release of dopamine.
ex.zh: 奖励会触发多巴胺的释放。

senses.en: Pleasure, especially from getting what you want.

ex.en: Children who could delay gratification did better at school.
ex.zh: 能够延迟满足的孩子在学校表现更好。

senses.en: To regret wrongdoing deeply and intend to behave better.

ex.en: He came to repent of lying to his closest friend.
ex.zh: 他后来为向自己最亲密的朋友撒谎而深感懊悔。

ex.en: Some argue that justice should allow offenders to repent and rebuild their lives through education and community service.
ex.zh: 有人认为，司法应让违法者有机会悔过，并通过教育和社区服务重建生活。

tip: 常用repent of sth；比regret更强调悔过。

senses.en: Responding less to a stimulus after repeated exposure.

ex.en: Habituation explains why we stop noticing a ticking clock.
ex.zh: 习惯化解释了为什么我们会不再注意钟表的滴答声。

senses.en: To make someone more aware of or responsive to something.

ex.en: Repeated pain can sensitize nerves.
ex.zh: 反复的疼痛会使神经变得敏感。

senses.en: Keeping unpleasant thoughts or feelings out of conscious awareness.

ex.en: Freud believed repression hides painful memories.
ex.zh: 弗洛伊德认为压抑会隐藏痛苦的记忆。

senses.en: a thick clear liquid used in medicines, foods, and skincare products

ex.en: This hand cream contains glycerin to keep skin soft.
ex.zh: 这款护手霜含有甘油，能让皮肤保持柔软。

ex.en: Manufacturers often add glycerin to skincare products because it helps retain moisture and prevent dryness.
ex.zh: 制造商常在护肤品中加入甘油，因为它有助于保持水分并防止干燥。

tip: 不可数名词；也拼作glycerine，化学名为glycerol。

senses.en: To give a reasonable-sounding explanation for behavior that has other causes.

ex.en: He rationalized his failure by blaming the test.
ex.zh: 他把失败归咎于考试来为自己找借口。

senses.en: A method of treating mental problems by exploring unconscious thoughts.

ex.en: Freud founded psychoanalysis in Vienna.
ex.zh: 弗洛伊德在维也纳创立了精神分析。

senses.en: A person who practices psychoanalysis.

ex.en: The psychoanalyst asked her about her dreams.
ex.zh: 精神分析师问起她的梦。

senses.en: To sleep lightly or be almost asleep.
A state of being partly asleep.

ex.en: Grandfather drowsed in his chair beside the sunny window.
ex.zh: 爷爷坐在阳光照进的窗边，在椅子上打瞌睡。

ex.en: Passengers may drowse during long journeys, making comfortable seating an important consideration for transport providers.
ex.zh: 乘客在长途旅行中可能会打瞌睡，因此舒适的座椅是交通服务商的重要考量。

col: drowse in a chair｜坐在椅子上打瞌睡
in a drowse｜处于半睡状态
tip: 较书面；日常说打瞌睡更常用doze。

senses.en: A theory that psychology should study only observable behavior.

ex.en: Behaviorism dominated American psychology for decades.
ex.zh: 行为主义曾主导美国心理学数十年。

senses.en: A psychologist who studies only observable behavior.

ex.en: The behaviorist trained pigeons to peck at shapes.
ex.zh: 行为主义者训练鸽子啄图形。

senses.en: To prevent something unwanted, or because of fearing it

ex.en: She whispered lest she wake the sleeping baby.
ex.zh: 她轻声说话，以免吵醒熟睡的婴儿。

ex.en: Policymakers should assess new technologies carefully lest short-term economic gains create lasting environmental problems.
ex.zh: 政策制定者应仔细评估新技术，以免短期经济收益造成长期环境问题。

col: lest we forget｜以免我们忘记
tip: 较正式；从句常用动词原形或should加原形。

senses.en: Focusing on human potential and personal growth.

ex.en: Humanistic psychology stresses free will.
ex.zh: 人本主义心理学强调自由意志。

senses.en: An organized whole that is seen as more than the sum of its parts.

ex.en: Gestalt psychologists studied how we see patterns.
ex.zh: 格式塔心理学家研究我们如何看出图案。

senses.en: The study of how the brain relates to behavior and thought.

ex.en: Neuropsychology examines patients with brain injuries.
ex.zh: 神经心理学研究脑损伤患者。

senses.en: To twist and squeeze something, especially to remove liquid.

ex.en: Wring out the wet towel before hanging it up.
ex.zh: 把湿毛巾拧干后再挂起来。

ex.en: Where washing machines are unavailable, residents must wring out heavy clothes by hand after washing.
ex.zh: 在没有洗衣机的地方，居民洗完厚重衣物后必须用手拧干。

col: wring out a towel｜拧干毛巾
wring your hands｜焦虑地绞着双手
wring water from clothes｜拧出衣服里的水
tip: 过去式和过去分词均为wrung；拧干常用wring out。

senses.en: A doctor or therapist who works directly with patients.

ex.en: Clinicians use interviews to assess anxiety.
ex.zh: 临床医生通过面谈评估焦虑。

senses.en: Anything that makes a behavior more likely to happen again.

ex.en: Praise is a powerful reinforcer for children.
ex.zh: 表扬对孩子来说是强有力的强化物。

senses.en: Experienced through another person rather than directly.

ex.en: She felt vicarious joy at her friend's success.
ex.zh: 她为朋友的成功感到感同身受的喜悦。

senses.en: To dishonestly take entrusted money or property for your own use.

ex.en: The treasurer misappropriated club funds to pay personal bills.
ex.zh: 财务主管挪用了俱乐部的资金来支付个人账单。

ex.en: Independent audits help prevent officials from misappropriating public funds intended for essential services such as healthcare and education.
ex.zh: 独立审计有助于防止官员挪用本应用于医疗、教育等基本服务的公共资金。

tip: 正式用语，常搭配funds，强调擅自挪作私用。

senses.en: A mental shortcut that helps make quick decisions.

ex.en: The availability heuristic makes us overestimate rare dangers.
ex.zh: 可得性启发法让我们高估罕见危险。

senses.en: A mental framework that organizes knowledge.

ex.en: A restaurant schema tells us what to expect when eating out.
ex.zh: “餐厅图式”告诉我们外出就餐时会发生什么。

senses.en: The inability to see things from another's point of view.

ex.en: Young children's egocentrism fades with age.
ex.zh: 幼儿的自我中心会随年龄减弱。

senses.en: Awkward in movement, shape or appearance.

ex.en: The young camel rose slowly on its ungainly legs.
ex.zh: 小骆驼用它那笨拙的长腿慢慢站了起来。

ex.en: Although early electric vehicles appeared ungainly, improvements in design have made them more attractive to consumers.
ex.zh: 虽然早期电动汽车外形笨拙，但设计上的改进使它们更能吸引消费者。

col: an ungainly shape｜不协调的外形
tip: 虽以-ly结尾，现代常用词性是形容词。

senses.en: Relating to both the senses and movement.

ex.en: Infants are in Piaget's sensorimotor stage.
ex.zh: 婴儿处于皮亚杰所说的感觉运动阶段。

senses.en: Relating to the stage of development when children think symbolically but not logically.

ex.en: Preoperational children believe a tall glass holds more water.
ex.zh: 前运算阶段的孩子认为高杯子装的水更多。

senses.en: The science of extracting metals and studying their properties.

ex.en: My cousin studies metallurgy and tests metals in a laboratory.
ex.zh: 我的表姐学习冶金学，在实验室检测金属。

ex.en: Advances in metallurgy have enabled manufacturers to develop lighter materials for more fuel-efficient vehicles.
ex.zh: 冶金技术的进步使制造商能够开发更轻的材料，用于制造更节能的车辆。

col: advances in metallurgy｜冶金技术的进步
tip: 不可数名词；从业专家称metallurgist。

senses.en: Rapid learning in young animals to follow the first moving thing they see.

ex.en: Lorenz's geese showed imprinting by following him.
ex.zh: 洛伦茨的小鹅跟着他走，表现出印刻现象。

senses.en: Tending to avoid closeness or difficult situations.

ex.en: An avoidant child shows little distress when the parent leaves.
ex.zh: 回避型的孩子在父母离开时几乎不难过。

senses.en: The degree to which a trait is passed on through genes.

ex.en: Twin studies estimate the heritability of intelligence.
ex.zh: 双胞胎研究估算智力的遗传度。

senses.en: a bird's feathers

ex.en: The parrot has bright plumage.
ex.zh: 这只鹦鹉羽毛鲜艳。

ex.en: Male birds often have brilliant plumage to attract females, while females are duller for camouflage.
ex.zh: 雄鸟常有艳丽的羽毛吸引雌鸟，雌鸟颜色较暗以便伪装。

tip: 性选择话题常见。

senses.en: The genetic makeup of an individual.

ex.en: Identical twins share the same genotype.
ex.zh: 同卵双胞胎拥有相同的基因型。

senses.en: The observable traits of an individual.

ex.en: Environment can change a person's phenotype.
ex.zh: 环境能改变一个人的表型。

senses.en: Relating to the upper middle part of the brain.

ex.en: The parietal lobe processes touch and space.
ex.zh: 顶叶处理触觉和空间信息。

senses.en: Destroy or remove something completely, leaving little or no trace.

ex.en: Heavy snowfall had obliterated every footprint on the garden path.
ex.zh: 大雪已将花园小路上的所有脚印彻底覆盖。

ex.en: Rapid urban development can obliterate historic neighbourhoods unless effective conservation measures are introduced early in the planning process.
ex.zh: 快速的城市开发可能彻底毁掉历史街区，除非在规划初期就引入有效的保护措施。

col: obliterate all traces｜抹去所有痕迹
tip: 是动词，强调彻底消除，比普通 remove 语气更强。

senses.en: Relating to the back part of the head or brain.

ex.en: Visual signals are processed mainly in the occipital lobe.
ex.zh: 视觉信号主要在枕叶中处理。

senses.en: A curved part of the brain that is important for forming memories.

ex.en: Damage to the hippocampus can make it hard to form new memories.
ex.zh: 海马体受损会使人难以形成新记忆。

senses.en: A small part of the brain that processes fear and other emotions.

ex.en: The amygdala reacts quickly to signs of danger.
ex.zh: 杏仁核会对危险信号迅速做出反应。

senses.en: To prove someone innocent or show that something was justified.

ex.en: The security footage vindicated the cleaner accused of stealing.
ex.zh: 监控录像证明了那位被指控偷窃的清洁工是无辜的。

ex.en: The significant decline in road accidents appears to vindicate the council's decision to introduce lower speed limits.
ex.zh: 交通事故显著减少，似乎证明市政委员会降低限速的决定是正确的。

col: vindicate a decision｜证明决定正确
vindicate an approach｜证明方法正确
feel vindicated｜感到自己得到证明
tip: 强调证据或结果证明正确，不只是口头辩护。

senses.en: A part of the brain that passes sensory signals to the cortex.

ex.en: The thalamus acts as a relay station for sensory information.
ex.zh: 丘脑是感觉信息的中继站。

senses.en: A small brain region that controls hunger, thirst, body temperature and hormones.

ex.en: The hypothalamus helps keep body temperature stable.
ex.zh: 下丘脑帮助维持体温稳定。

senses.en: A toxic, flammable liquid hydrocarbon used in chemical manufacturing.

ex.en: The technician tested the water for traces of benzene.
ex.zh: 技术人员检测了水中是否有微量苯。

ex.en: Strict controls on industrial emissions can reduce workers' exposure to benzene and other harmful chemicals.
ex.zh: 严格控制工业排放可以减少工人接触苯及其他有害化学物质的机会。

tip: 苯是有毒化合物；勿与汽油的英式说法petrol混淆。

senses.en: The part at the back of the brain that controls balance and movement.

ex.en: The cerebellum coordinates fine movements such as writing.
ex.zh: 小脑协调写字等精细动作。

senses.en: The lowest part of the brain, which controls breathing and heartbeat.

ex.en: The brainstem controls functions we never think about, like breathing.
ex.zh: 脑干控制着呼吸这类我们从不去想的功能。

senses.en: The long thin part of a nerve cell that carries signals away from it.

ex.en: Signals travel along the axon to the next neuron.
ex.zh: 信号沿轴突传到下一个神经元。

senses.en: To praise someone or something very highly.
To raise someone to a higher rank or position.

ex.en: Her songs exalt the beauty of ordinary life.
ex.zh: 她的歌曲颂扬平凡生活中的美。

ex.en: Public monuments often exalt national heroes while overlooking the contributions of ordinary citizens.
ex.zh: 公共纪念碑往往颂扬民族英雄，却忽视普通公民的贡献。

col: exalt the virtues of｜盛赞……的美德
exalt someone to a position｜将某人提升至某职位
tip: 正式用词；指高度颂扬，不是普通的表扬。

senses.en: A short branch of a nerve cell that receives signals from other cells.

ex.en: Each neuron may have thousands of dendrites.
ex.zh: 每个神经元可能有数千个树突。

senses.en: The small gap where a signal passes from one nerve cell to another.

ex.en: Learning strengthens the synapses between neurons.
ex.zh: 学习会加强神经元之间的突触。

senses.en: A fatty layer around nerve fibers that makes signals travel faster.

ex.en: Myelin allows nerve impulses to move much more quickly.
ex.zh: 髓鞘使神经冲动传得快得多。

senses.en: The chest, especially a woman's, or the embrace it provides.
Very close and trusted, used mainly before friend.

ex.en: The grandmother held the sleepy child to her bosom.
ex.zh: 祖母把困倦的孩子搂在怀里。

ex.en: Traditional paintings often depict a parent holding a child to their bosom, symbolising protection and affection.
ex.zh: 传统绘画常描绘父母将孩子搂在怀中的情景，象征着保护与关爱。

col: hold someone to one's bosom｜将某人搂在怀里
in the bosom of the family｜在家庭的温暖怀抱中
tip: 较文学化或旧式；bosom friend指知心朋友。

senses.en: A hormone released by the body in response to stress.

ex.en: Cortisol levels rise when people feel under pressure.
ex.zh: 人感到有压力时皮质醇水平会升高。

senses.en: A process in which repeated exposure makes a response stronger.

ex.en: Sensitization can make a person react more strongly to a repeated noise.
ex.zh: 敏感化会使人对反复出现的噪音反应更强。

senses.en: Describing behavior that is shaped by its consequences, such as rewards.

ex.en: In operant conditioning, a rat learns to press a lever for food.
ex.zh: 在操作性条件反射中，老鼠学会按杠杆获取食物。

senses.en: In a cheerful and lively way.
With bright, cheerful colours.

ex.en: The children laughed gaily as they chased bubbles outside.
ex.zh: 孩子们在外面追逐泡泡，欢快地笑着。

ex.en: Gaily decorated streets can attract visitors during local festivals and encourage spending in nearby shops.
ex.zh: 当地节庆期间，装饰鲜艳的街道能够吸引游客，促进周边商店的消费。

tip: 略带文学色彩；也可形容装饰色彩鲜艳。
